title: Terraform Modules and Reuse
subtitle: Reusable Terraform patterns with module inputs, outputs, standards, and version safety

mapResources.label: Open Modules and Reuse Lab README

nodes.label: Module
nodes.definition: A module is a reusable Terraform configuration package.
nodes.whyItMatters: Modules help teams avoid copying the same Terraform code repeatedly.
nodes.safeSentence: A module packages Terraform code so an infrastructure pattern can be reused.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not think modules automatically make code good. Bad modules can hide complexity.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Modules are Terraform's reuse mechanism. They package configuration so teams can call the same pattern with different inputs.

note.summary:
A module is a reusable Terraform building block.

Root module: calls a standard module.
Child module: contains the reusable implementation.

image.caption: Root module calls child modules with inputs and receives outputs for safer reuse.

nodes.label: Root Module
nodes.definition: The root module is the Terraform configuration in the directory where Terraform is run.
nodes.whyItMatters: Every Terraform run has a root module, even if no child modules are used.
nodes.safeSentence: The root module is the main Terraform configuration for the current run.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not assume root module means a shared reusable module. It simply means the current entry point.
nodes.interviewAnswer: The root module is the main Terraform configuration being executed.

note.summary: The folder where you run Terraform is the root module. It may call child modules or define resources directly.

nodes.label: Child Module
nodes.definition: A child module is a module called by another module.
nodes.whyItMatters: Child modules let teams compose larger infrastructure from reusable parts.
nodes.safeSentence: A child module is a reusable package called by the root module or another module.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not bury too much logic in child modules until nobody understands what they do.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Child modules let teams reuse common infrastructure patterns while passing in environment-specific values.

nodes.label: Module Inputs
nodes.definition: Module inputs are variables passed into a module.
nodes.whyItMatters: Inputs let the same module behave differently for different environments or use cases.
nodes.safeSentence: Module inputs let a reusable module accept different values.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not create modules with too many confusing inputs.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Module inputs are variables that let callers customize reusable Terraform patterns.

note.summary: Same module, different inputs for dev/prod. This connects directly to the Variables map.

nodes.label: Module Outputs
nodes.definition: Module outputs expose useful values from inside a module.
nodes.whyItMatters: Outputs let the calling configuration use values created inside the module.
nodes.safeSentence: Module outputs let other Terraform code use results from a module.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not expose sensitive values casually through module outputs.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Module outputs return useful values such as IDs, names, ARNs, URLs, or other resource attributes created inside the module.

nodes.label: Module Source
nodes.definition: Module source tells Terraform where to find the module.
nodes.whyItMatters: Modules can come from local paths, Git repositories, registries, or other supported locations.
nodes.safeSentence: Module source identifies where Terraform should load the module from.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not pull unreviewed module code blindly into important environments.
nodes.interviewAnswer: The module source tells Terraform whether the module comes from a local folder, registry, or versioned repository.

note.summary: Examples: local path, Git URL, Terraform registry source.

nodes.label: Reuse
nodes.definition: Reuse means calling the same Terraform pattern in multiple places instead of copying code.
nodes.whyItMatters: Reuse reduces duplication and helps teams standardize infrastructure.
nodes.safeSentence: Modules reduce copy/paste by making common infrastructure patterns reusable.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not create a module too early if the pattern has not repeated yet.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Modules are useful when a Terraform pattern repeats or needs consistent implementation across environments or teams.

note.summary: Good candidates: standard buckets, IAM patterns, tagging, monitoring scaffolds.

nodes.label: Standards
nodes.definition: Modules can encode naming, tagging, security, and environment conventions.
nodes.whyItMatters: Standards help teams produce consistent infrastructure.
nodes.safeSentence: Modules can help teams bake standards into reusable infrastructure patterns.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not let standards become hidden magic that users cannot understand.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Modules can standardize things like naming, tags, encryption settings, retention policies, or required monitoring patterns.

note.summary: Consistency examples: owner tags, retention defaults, naming policy.

nodes.label: Versioning
nodes.definition: Module versioning controls which release of a module a caller uses.
nodes.whyItMatters: Versioning helps teams adopt module changes safely.
nodes.safeSentence: Versioning protects teams from surprise module changes.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not point production blindly at a moving branch without understanding the risk.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Shared modules should be versioned so changes can be tested and adopted intentionally.

note.summary: Safer pattern: pin versions, test lower envs, then promote.

nodes.label: Module Risk
nodes.definition: Module risk is the danger that reusable Terraform code hides complexity or causes broad impact when changed.
nodes.whyItMatters: A bad module can spread bad patterns everywhere it is reused.
nodes.safeSentence: Modules are powerful, but they need design, review, and version discipline.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not treat modules as black boxes that nobody reviews.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Modules help reuse, but teams need to review them carefully because changes can affect many environments.

note.summary: Risks: unclear outputs, hidden resources, weak versioning, poor docs.

nodes.label: Variables, Outputs, and Locals
nodes.definition: Open the previous map that explains Terraform inputs, internal values, and outputs.
nodes.whyItMatters: Modules depend heavily on variables and outputs.
nodes.safeSentence: Modules are easier to understand after variables, locals, and outputs make sense.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not treat this as a module concept. It is a map doorway.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Modules build on variables and outputs because inputs customize the module and outputs expose results to the caller.
